summary: Count by rote to 20, and say which number (1 to 10) comes next when counting.
Count up to 10 objects set out in a neat arrangement, touching each one once.
Say how many are in a group by giving the last number counted.
See how many are in a small group, up to 5, and name it without counting.
Compare two groups of objects and say if one has more, less or the same.
Name written numbers from 0 to 10 and match each one to a counted group.
Read some written numbers up to 10 and start writing a few of them.
Use first, second and third to say where someone or something is in a line.
Spot, copy, continue and make up simple repeating patterns, like red-red-blue.
Solve simple adding and taking-away problems with objects or fingers in play and daily life.
Sort objects by one feature, then sort them again by another and say why, with help.
Describe how big, long or heavy things are with comparing words like long, longer, longest.
Compare a few objects and put them in order by length or weight.
Say what simple measuring tools, like a ruler or a scale, are used for.
Measure things by lining up copies of one small object, like paper clips, with help.
Name circles, squares, triangles and rectangles whatever their size or which way they turn.
Describe flat and solid shapes, like a square has four sides and a ball rolls.
Make and build shapes out of materials, like making a square from craft sticks.
Understand and use position words for place, direction and distance, like above, behind, near.
